articles.title: China’s Oil Imports from Persian Gulf Jump to Wartime High
articles.description: China’s crude oil imports from the Persian Gulf surged by 42.4% in October from September, to the highest level since the Iran war began, as supply via the Strait of Hormuz rebounded and Gulf producers slashed prices for their crude to attract buyers amid record-high freight rates. China imported 19.7 million tons of crude oil from the Persian Gulf producers, excluding Iran, in October, a 42.4% jump from the previous month, per calculations by the South China Morning Post based on Chinese customs data released on Friday. October…

articles.title: Historic Superpower Summit Delivers Big Promises but Few Breakthroughs
articles.description: US President Donald Trump, Chinese leader Xi Jinping, and Russian President Vladimir Putin held a historic meeting on the sidelines of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) summit in Shenzhen that delivered modest wins for all three men but no game-changing accords. The high-stakes summit on November 19 marked the first time the current heads of state of the three world’s largest nuclear powers have held a trilateral meeting without other leaders present, though Putin and Xi have met about 50 times. articles.description: At least two Norwegian energy companies have reported a cyberattack or an attempted one around the same time this week.

articles.title: Europe Has Already Drained 11% of Its Summer Gas Injections
articles.description: In less than a month, Europe has already sapped 11% of the natural gas volumes it had injected into storage during the summer, which, combined with a low starting point of gas in storage, intensifies concerns about winter supply. So far into the heating season, which officially began at the end of October, the net withdrawals of European countries have reached about 11% of the 51.2 billion cubic meters of gas they had injected into storage sites this summer, Azeri outlet APA-Economics reported on Friday, quoting data from Gas Infrastructure…

articles.title: India’s LPG Consumption Hits 8-Month High as Supply Rebounds
articles.description: India’s consumption of liquefied petroleum gas (LPG) jumped to the highest level in eight months in October as supply has gradually recovered after the shock loss of shipments from the Middle East earlier this year. India’s demand for LPG, its primary cooking fuel, rose to 2.6 million tons in October, according to government data cited by local outlet Mint. LPG consumption last month hit the highest level since February, when India’s demand was 2.8 million tons just before the war began. Amid recovering supply, India’s LPG…

articles.title: Gulf Sees Iran Oil Movement as US Widens Blockade
articles.description: A cargo of Iranian crude was transferred between two tankers in the Persian Gulf this week, as the US warned its forces could target vessels that carry out the practice while enforcing a maritime blockade.

articles.title: Trump’s Ukraine Energy Truce Unravels as Russian Missiles Hit Kyiv
articles.description: Politics, Geopolitics & Conflict Trump’s October “energy truce” between Russia and Ukraine in October is over, and Vladimir Putin has taken a new one off the table. After meeting Trump and Xi at the APEC summit on Thursday, Putin said Russia would not negotiate after Ukraine’s strikes on the Crimean Bridge. articles.title: Iraq's Oil Crackdown Sparks New Showdown With Kurdistan
articles.description: Iraq’s federal government is using its oil-smuggling case against the pro-Iranian militia Kata’ib Hezbollah south of Baghdad to force the Kurdistan Regional Government in the north to hand over more oil and open its fields to federal inspectors. South of Baghdad, the Iraqi PM has ordered federal forces to take over a pipeline at Jurf al-Sakhar (Babil province) that the pro-Iranian militia has been illegally tapping into since at least 2021. Iraqi officials estimate the group made away with hundreds of millions of dollars in crude. Baghdad…

articles.title: WTI Crude Sinks More Than 5% as Global Oil Glut Fears Grow
articles.description: The oil market spent the week weighing an increase in global supply against the risk of further disruptions in the Middle East. More crude is reaching buyers from the region, while U.S. inventories are building. Attacks on tankers and energy infrastructure remain a threat, but they have not been enough to stop the decline in prices. For now, the supply story appears to be winning. January West Texas Intermediate crude oil futures are down more than 5% for the week. The decline suggests traders are putting more weight on the barrels reaching the…

articles.title: Iran Steps Up Hormuz Tanker Attacks as Oil Prices Slide
articles.description: Iran has intensified attacks on tankers in the Strait of Hormuz in recent weeks, just as crude oil flows from the Persian Gulf recover and oil prices fall amid expectations of oversupply within months. The number of attacks soared in October to the highest level since the Iran war began at the end of February, and has continued at nearly daily occurrences so far in November, according to data compiled by Bloomberg. Meanwhile, crude oil volumes flowing from the Strait of Hormuz have declined in recent days, although it’s unclear if this is…

articles.title: Iran Refuses Nuclear Inspections as U.S. Military Threats Mount
articles.description: Iran has warned once again that it would not grant access to its nuclear sites and materials to UN inspectors amid continued U.S. threats of military strikes, a senior Iranian official was quoted as saying on Friday. “We will not accept being bombed on the one hand while being asked in a tone of entitlement, on the other, to provide detailed information about our materials and sites and grant unrestricted access to them,” Reza Najafi, Iran’s ambassador to international organizations in Vienna, told the International Atomic…

articles.title: China’s Solar Exports Surge 21% as U.S. Tariff Deadline Looms
articles.description: Chinese exports of solar cells jumped in October for the second consecutive month as importers are stocking up ahead of new U.S. tariffs on polysilicon coming into effect on December 4. China’s solar cell exports soared by 21% year-over-year to 1.55 billion units in October, Bloomberg reported on Friday, citing data from China’s General Administration of Customs. October was the second month in a row in which Chinese solar cell shipments overseas rose from a year earlier, after four consecutive months of declines between May and August…

articles.title: Iran Moves to Restart Oil Exports Despite U.S. Naval Blockade
articles.description: Iran is preparing to relaunch crude oil exports even as the United States says it is going to tighten the naval blockade on Iranian ports it imposed earlier this year in response to Iran’s closing of the Strait of Hormuz. Bloomberg reported earlier today that a cargo of Iranian crude had been transferred from a Suezmax tanker under U.S. sanctions to a medium-range vessel that is not under sanctions. The information comes from an anti-Iran organization named United Against Nuclear Iran and vessel tracker Kpler. A Reuters report cited TankerTrackers.com…

articles.title: Senate Passes Sweeping Energy Permitting Reform Bill in 62-33 Vote
articles.description: The Senate has passed the Bipartisan American Affordability and Jobs Bill that aims to speed up the approval process for large-scale energy projects, including new power plants, grid upgrades, and data centers. Senators voted 62-33 for the bill, with the majority of Republican Senators supporting the bill and getting joined by 14 Democrat Senators and one independent. The bill is now headed for the House. articles.title: Oil Prices Rebound as Houthi Attacks Reignite Middle East Supply Fears
articles.description: Crude oil prices earlier today reversed a decline that began earlier in the week, gaining on reports of fresh Houthi attacks on Saudi targets and continued tanker trouble in the Strait of Hormuz. articles.description: Oil prices fluctuated as renewed Iran tensions offset improving Middle East supplies.

articles.title: TPAO In Talks for $1B Loan
articles.description: Turkey's state-owned oil and natural gas producer is in talks with banks for a loan of up to $1 billion, according to people familiar with the matter.

articles.title: Canada Builds an Energy Exit From the U.S.
articles.description: Canada is building an energy export industry for a world beyond the tariff-chasing United States. In 2024, the U.S. bought all but 0.01% of Canada’s natural gas exports. Ottawa now wants 55% of those exports to go to other countries by the mid-2030s, and Germany’s state-owned Uniper has signed a 20-year deal for liquefied natural gas from a planned British Columbia terminal.
